g.text: SEE ALONE ("routine check, family wait outside") → ASK kindly ("do you feel safe? who hurts/
frightens you?") → EXAMINE (body map injuries, photos per protocol, verbatim quotes) →
PROTECT (admit if unsafe, never confront abuser with elder present) → REPORT (in-charge +
Social Welfare + DOVVSU/police — Acts 560/732, PRO-I M4/M6: protection beats secrecy) →
FOLLOW UP (review date, safe discharge only). Witchcraft accusations = abuse + refer.
END-OF-LIFE ESSENTIALS: recognise dying (surprise question: "would I be surprised
if they died in 12 months?" — if NO, plan!) → goals talk (where? who? what matters? DNAR
discussed + documented per policy — PRO-I M2) → palliate (pain ladder M03 + breathlessness
+ secretions + nausea + agitation + mouth care) → comfort (family present, prayers, light,
position, sips if wanted) → after (verify death per protocol, wash + honour rituals, belongings
listed, family grief + practical help, staff debrief).
ADVANCE CARE PLANS: wishes written while capacitous (place, funeral, who decides) —
reviewed yearly; capacity assessed per decision (PRO-I M2/M4); family guided ("what would
THEY want?"), futile CPR avoided by conversation not surprise. Stopping burdens (dialysis,
admissions, tubes) with consent + comfort = care, not killing — document reasoning.
Nurse's dying-patient checklist: pain 0–3? breath settled? mouth moist? family called?
prayers offered? rituals known? belongings safe? juniors supported? self debriefed? —
good deaths are NURSED, not happened. Coroner/reportable rules (PRO-I M6) still apply;
expected deaths need doctor certification + family tenderness in equal measure.
Exam line: \"see alone, ask kindly, protect first, report always — and nurse good deaths.\"
